pests.image_description: Field photograph associated with Coconut rhinoceros beetle
pests.image_credit: Slunky / iNaturalist, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
pests.affected_part: Crown, spear leaves, and young palms
pests.characteristic_signs: V-shaped frond cuts, holes in the crown, damaged growing point
ai_recommendations: Maintain routine scouting and compare the same palms at the next inspection.
Inspect the crown and unopened spear leaves for fresh V-shaped cuts and boring damage.
Remove or properly manage decaying logs, manure piles, and other breeding material near the farm.
Use monitoring or pheromone traps only according to current local agricultural guidance.
Report clustered or severe damage to the Philippine Coconut Authority or local agriculture office.
pests.formula: score = 100 × logistic(prior log-odds + climate + tree vulnerability + farm-condition deficit + symptom evidence - management protection)

pests.image_description: Field photograph associated with Coconut scale insect
pests.image_credit: Gilles San Martin, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons; representative scale-insect photograph
pests.characteristic_signs: White scale colonies, chlorosis, drying leaves, weakened crown
ai_recommendations: Maintain routine scouting and compare the same palms at the next inspection.
Inspect the underside of fronds and nearby palms for white scale colonies and yellowing.
Avoid transporting infested leaves or planting material to unaffected areas.
Conserve natural enemies and avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum pesticide use.
Seek PCA or LGU confirmation before applying any registered control product.
pests.formula: score = 100 × logistic(prior log-odds + climate + tree vulnerability + farm-condition deficit + symptom evidence - management protection)

pests.image_description: Field photograph associated with Coconut leaf beetle
pests.image_credit: Cameron Brumley, DAFWA, CC BY 3.0 AU, via Wikimedia Commons
pests.affected_part: Unopened spear leaves and young fronds
pests.characteristic_signs: Brown feeding scars, damaged spear leaves, reduced leaf opening
ai_recommendations: Maintain routine scouting and compare the same palms at the next inspection.
Inspect unopened spear leaves for feeding scars, larvae, or adult beetles.
Remove and safely dispose of heavily infested leaf material when advised by extension personnel.
Protect parasitoids and other biological-control agents used in local programs.
Prioritize young palms because severe spear-leaf damage can slow establishment.
pests.formula: score = 100 × logistic(prior log-odds + climate + tree vulnerability + farm-condition deficit + symptom evidence - management protection)

pests.image_description: Field photograph associated with Coconut mealybug complex
pests.image_credit: Nayana.sondi; public-domain representative mealybug photograph, via Wikimedia Commons
pests.affected_part: Leaf axils, tender shoots, and developing nuts
pests.characteristic_signs: White waxy colonies, honeydew, ants, sooty mold
ai_recommendations: Maintain routine scouting and compare the same palms at the next inspection.
Inspect leaf axils and tender tissues for white waxy insects, honeydew, and sooty mold.
Monitor and manage ant activity because ants can protect sap-feeding pests from natural enemies.
Improve sanitation and avoid moving infested planting material.
Confirm the pest and any registered treatment with local extension or PCA personnel.
pests.formula: score = 100 × logistic(prior log-odds + climate + tree vulnerability + farm-condition deficit + symptom evidence - management protection)

pests.image_description: Field photograph associated with Red palm weevil
pests.image_credit: gailhampshire, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
pests.characteristic_signs: Bore holes, chewed fibers, oozing sap, crown collapse
ai_recommendations: Maintain routine scouting and compare the same palms at the next inspection.
Inspect wounds, trunk bases, and crowns for holes, fermented odor, fibers, or oozing sap.
Avoid unnecessary trunk injuries and seal or manage fresh wounds according to local guidance.
Use approved monitoring traps where a local surveillance program exists.
Isolate and report severely affected palms promptly because internal damage may be advanced before symptoms appear.
pests.formula: score = 100 × logistic(prior log-odds + climate + tree vulnerability + farm-condition deficit + symptom evidence - management protection)

pests.image_description: Field photograph associated with Coconut leaf miner
pests.image_credit: C. L. Staines / USDA; public-domain photograph, via Wikimedia Commons
pests.characteristic_signs: Linear mines, translucent tracks, browning of mined leaf tissue
ai_recommendations: Maintain routine scouting and compare the same palms at the next inspection.
Inspect leaflets for narrow mines or transparent feeding tracks.
Record the fraction of affected fronds and whether damage is increasing between inspections.
Protect natural enemies and avoid unnecessary pesticide applications that may disrupt them.
Submit samples or clear photographs to extension personnel when identification is uncertain.
pests.formula: score = 100 × logistic(prior log-odds + climate + tree vulnerability + farm-condition deficit + symptom evidence - management protection)

pests.image_description: Field photograph associated with Coconut eriophyid mite
pests.image_credit: Hartford H. Keifer; public-domain coconut mite damage photograph, via Wikimedia Commons
pests.characteristic_signs: Corky triangular scars, distorted nuts, premature nut fall
ai_recommendations: Maintain routine scouting and compare the same palms at the next inspection.
Inspect young nuts beneath the perianth for corky scars, deformation, and premature drop.
Maintain balanced nutrition and reduce prolonged moisture stress where possible.
Remove badly damaged fallen nuts from the immediate monitoring area.
Consult agricultural extension personnel before considering any registered acaricide treatment.
pests.formula: score = 100 × logistic(prior log-odds + climate + tree vulnerability + farm-condition deficit + symptom evidence - management protection)

pests.image_description: Field photograph associated with Coconut black-headed caterpillar
pests.image_credit: Close-up larval reference from ICAR-National Bureau of Agricultural Insect Resources (NBAIR)
pests.image_license: External reference image; copyright remains with ICAR-NBAIR
pests.characteristic_signs: Silken galleries, brown patches, frass, progressive defoliation
ai_recommendations: Maintain baseline monitoring; the current conditions do not indicate a high outbreak signal.
Inspect lower fronds for silk galleries, dried leaflet patches, larvae, and frass.
Remove heavily damaged fronds only when agronomically justified; excessive pruning can further weaken palms.
Conserve parasitoids and predators and coordinate area-wide monitoring when outbreaks cluster.
Escalate expanding defoliation to the local agriculture office for identification and control advice.

annual_by_product.coverage_label: partial year from selected start date

extreme_events.label: Heat stress
extreme_events.impact_summary: Peak severity 57.5/100; estimated loss 0.31 t (14.2% of the event-period baseline) across 5 week(s). Approximately 103 trees may require inspection.

source.title: Non-Food and Industrial Crops: Volume of Production, by Region, Province, Quarter, and Semester, 2010-2026
source.official_note: Final data through Quarter 4, Semester 2, and Annual 2025; preliminary Quarter 1 2026.
source.gap_method: Unavailable cells are estimated from location-specific seasonal shares and annual interpolation/extrapolation. Estimated cells are tagged estimated_gap and are not represented as official observations.

farm_site_forecast.label: Hybrid farm outlook: short-term provider forecast when available, followed by a plausible climate-conditioned projection
farm_site_forecast.production_label: Weekly production equivalents are partitioned into Coconut Mature and Coconut Young categories using official provincial seasonality plus distinct weather-response equations.

product_model.identity: Coconut with husk = Coconut Mature + Coconut Young
product_model.mature_response: Base mature share × exp(water support + temperature support + condition - drought - heat - wind - excess rain - pest pressure)
product_model.young_response: Base young share × exp(stronger water and humidity support - stronger drought, heat, wind, excess-rain and pest penalties)
product_model.normalization: The two weather-adjusted category weights are normalized every week to conserve total husked production.

data_mode_explanation.deterministic_short_term_forecast: Real numerical weather-model output aggregated to local calendar days; still a forecast, not an observation.
data_mode_explanation.plausible_stochastic_climate_simulation: Climate-conditioned generated weather path used after the numerical forecast horizon; not an exact prediction.

warnings: Only dates tagged deterministic_short_term_forecast use current provider model output; later dates are simulated possibilities.
Long-term colored weather fields are model-generated visualizations, not future radar or satellite images.
Daily and weekly production equivalents are allocations of annual simulated production, not a guaranteed harvest for an exact date.
PSA provincial production observations calibrate the three product series; unavailable periods are explicitly tagged as estimates in provenance.
limitations: Transition and intervention parameters require calibration with verified longitudinal coconut-farm records.
Long-term typhoon exposure is sampled probabilistically and does not predict exact storm dates.
Within-farm differences are not inferred unless measured spatial inputs are supplied.
Reference productive-palm and health shares are provisional development assumptions that require field calibration.
